minutes.headline: Open Space Committee reelected its chair and began rewriting land-acquisition criteria, to return in October
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Open Space Committee held its first meeting since June, approved the May minutes, and re-elected its officers (Mike Hill as chair, Anna as vice chair, Eric as clerk) under a new term-limit bylaw. Most of the meeting was spent workshopping proposed revisions to the open space acquisition criteria -- parcel size tiers, habitat resources, public access, scenic vistas, contiguous parcels, and agricultural viability -- with the chair agreeing to rework the wording based on member feedback and bring it back in October.

what_happened.line: The committee re-elected Mike Hill as chair, Anna as vice chair, and Eric as clerk, each by unanimous roll call under a newly adopted term-limit bylaw.

Members spent most of the meeting workshopping revisions to the criteria used to prioritize land for open space acquisition, including parcel size, habitat, public access, scenic vistas, contiguous parcels, and farmland viability.
No vote was taken on the criteria; the chair agreed to rework the wording based on member feedback and bring a revised draft back in October.

The chair will check with the conservation commission, planning board, and parks department on whether their appointed representatives to this committee will continue, since the new bylaw sets term limits and a reappointment process.

why_it_matters: The criteria under revision are what the town uses to decide which parcels get prioritized for conservation purchase or protection, so the wording adopted in October will shape future land decisions.
The new term-limit bylaw affects who can serve on the committee and how other boards appoint their representatives to it.

meetings.headline: Committee votes to recommend against acquiring 35 Lemonster Road; begins push for a town conservation fund
meetings.summary: The Open Space Committee, now an official standing committee under the town bylaw, heard a proposal from the town planning director to seek a small recurring annual town meeting appropriation for a conservation fund, modeled on a neighboring town's practice, to build capacity for future land purchases and grant matches. The committee voted to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on a 35 Lemonster Road parcel after reviewing it against acquisition criteria, and discussed revising those criteria and pursuing agricultural preservation restrictions on several parcels considered at risk of development.

The committee voted to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on a 35 Lemonster Road parcel after reviewing it against acquisition criteria, and discussed revising those criteria and pursuing agricultural preservation restrictions on several parcels considered at risk of development.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously to recommend the Select Board not exercise the town's right of first refusal on the 35 Lemonster Road parcel.
The planning director proposed asking future town meetings for a small recurring appropriation to build a dedicated conservation fund.
Members agreed to first consult the treasurer/collector and town manager on the steps to set up such a fund, targeting the fall town meeting to create it and the following annual meeting to fund it.

Revised acquisition criteria and any agricultural preservation restrictions would shape which private parcels the town moves to protect from development going forward.

Moving appointing authority to the select board changes which elected body residents hold accountable for who sits on the committee.
Whether the agriculture commission gets a dedicated seat or the seat goes at-large affects who represents farming interests on open-space decisions.
